doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Thunderbird opening in Las Vegas on a day's notice
summary: A chance meeting with Don Palmer leads to an emergency opening at the Thunderbird, then honoring their Mr. Kelly's contract.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: On the road again. But I think the next major thing that happened was then we went to Vegas to visit a friend of ours who lived there. And we were on our way to Chicago to work at Mr. Kelly’s in Chicago. And so we had the kids in the car and everything, and we went to Las Vegas to visit this friend, and we saw him, we stayed a few days, and one day we bumped into this guy on the street, who used to be Charlie Ventura’s manager, Don Palmer. And Don Palmer says, “what are you doing here?” And we said we’re just on our way to Chicago, we stopped to see a friend. Well, he says, “listen, this is funny but you know there’s a group that was supposed to open at the Thunderbird and they were in an automobile accident and they can’t open tomorrow night, so could you open?” And we said, “we don’t have a group here or anything, no, we’re on our way to Chicago.” He says, “well if you could do this for me, it might be very good for you guys, because © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
maybe you’ll get something through them hearing you, you know, maybe you’ll get a contract to come back or something.” So we said well— he sai, “I’ll get you a bass player and drummer.”
I’ll get you your rhythm section.

He say, “we’ll get a rhythm section, you’ll rehearse one time or you’ll get together tomorrow and open tomorrow night.” And we said well okay. We had to arrange with the kids, I don’t remember even what we did.
We found an apartment somewhere, just bang, get in there, get in there, rehearse, open up at the Thunderbird.
A rented apartment, furnished you know.

And we were there for two weeks, and it created a stir because we were doing something totally different than the usual front line, who learns how to do dance steps. And we were playing what we do. And I think at one time we had Carl Fontana join us on trombone, and we had a great group. And after the two weeks we had to go to Mr. Kelly’s to do our contracted job there. And I told the manager, I said we have to leave to go Mr. Kelly’s and do our two weeks over there. And he says you can’t leave.

I said well wait a minute. I said I didn’t have a contract with you, we’re here, we’re doing a job for you, we have a contract with Mr. Kelly’s. I said I believe in honoring the contract. After two weeks he says, you go do two weeks and you’re back here. I said why not. It was wonderful. So we came back and we stayed a year. Now by this time we bought a house, we rented one and then we bought a different house, and got the kids in school.
